cohort: The study included 132 women at term, comprising 52 receiving epidural analgesia for vaginal delivery and 80 receiving spinal anesthesia for cesarean delivery.
finding: Phenylephrine-based vasopressor management during spinal anesthesia resulted in higher blood pressure and systemic vascular resistance index but lower cardiac index and heart rate compared to ephedrine-based management, which tended to preserve cardiac index through chronotropic effects.
mod_finding: Cardiac index remained stable and comparable between women receiving epidural analgesia for vaginal delivery and those receiving spinal anesthesia for cesarean delivery, though stroke volume was higher in the EA group and heart rate was higher in the SA group.
